reasoning_steps.argument: Let S denote developmental stage, E an animal's early wound-response measurement, and L its later basal-epidermal RIC/ECM activation measurement. An animal-level coupling claim concerns the joint distribution P(E,L|S), for example beta_s = Cov(E,L|S=s)/Var(E|S=s), when the variance is nonzero. Separate destructive collections at early and late times generally estimate only the marginals P(E|S) and P(L|S). Matching stage, batch, or clutch does not turn different animals into repeated measurements.
reasoning_steps.title: Define the estimand that a temporal-coupling claim needs

reasoning_steps.argument: Take two stage classes and let E equal -1 or +1 with probability one half in each. In model U, set L=E at both stages; both slopes equal +1, so the late-minus-early-stage slope contrast is 0. In model V, set L=E at the first stage and L=-E at the second; the slopes are +1 and -1, giving a contrast of -2. At every stage in both models, E and L separately have the same symmetric two-point distribution, with mean 0 and variance 1. Thus all unpaired marginal observations have identical distributions under U and V, although the proposed coupling interaction differs. Increasing the number of unpaired samples cannot distinguish these models. This is a constructed statistical example, not simulated or observed frog data.

A stage-by-time expression contrast can therefore be real and reproducible without identifying within-animal coupling. Likewise, a correlation across a few stage/time group means is an ecological association, not an estimate of beta_s. Predominantly regenerative scRNA-seq can help define candidate cell states, but cannot supply missing refractory observations or reconstruct individual early-to-late pairing without additional validated information.

No such intervention or outcome is established here.

reasoning_steps.argument: Within one stage, let U be uniform on [0,1]. Model I assigns E=U and R=U; Model II assigns E=U and R=1−U. reasoning_steps.argument: Let E_s(t) denote measured basal-epidermal ERK activity at stage s, C_s(t) denote receptivity to enter the transient regenerative epidermal state, and J_s = k∫E_s(t)C_s(t)dt denote cumulative transition drive, with k > 0. Downstream state occupancy R and remodeling M can be represented by dR/dt = kEC − δ_R R and dM/dt = aR − δ_M M. Model A_amp attributes stage-46 failure to insufficient early E, with C concentrated in the early window at both stages. Model B_delay retains early receptivity at stage 40 but places stage-46 receptivity in the late window. These are deliberately restricted alternatives; broad 'failure to induce RICs' includes both and cannot itself be distinguished by this experiment.
reasoning_steps.title: Define the two restricted competing mechanisms

reasoning_steps.argument: Let p_early and p_late be nonnegative added ERK-activity pulses supported on the respective windows and having the same positive integral Q. Within stage 46, J_late − J_early = k∫C_46(t)[p_late(t) − p_early(t)]dt, because the untreated trajectory cancels. In the idealized A_amp model, C_46 equals c > 0 in the early window and zero in the late window, so the contrast is −kcQ. In B_delay the supports are reversed, giving +kcQ. Thus the sign differs without requiring a difference in total added ERK activity. For nonrectangular receptive windows the contrast measures the pulse-weighted difference in receptivity; its sign is not guaranteed merely by naming a mechanism. A monotone, nonsaturated relationship between transition drive and regrowth transfers this sign to the expected regrowth contrast. Saturation, zero receptivity in both windows or an independent downstream block can erase discrimination.
reasoning_steps.title: Derive the pulse-timing discrimination

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed stage-46 rescue uses a light-gated RAF/ERK actuator expressed specifically in basal epidermis, comparing early versus late activation. A separate validation cohort must establish expression specificity, ERK activation kinetics, reversibility and noninjurious illumination. Actuator availability and efficacy in these cells are unverified. Measured epidermal ERK trajectories, rather than light duration, define exposure; pulse amplitude and integral should be matched within a preregistered tolerance, provisionally 10%. If endogenous early activity is already near saturation, a larger early light dose is not an adequate matched-exposure control. Failure to achieve comparable perturbations makes the biological contrast uninterpretable and stops the efficacy experiment.
reasoning_steps.title: Specify a feasible intervention class without claiming an available validated reagent

reasoning_steps.argument: At stage 40, transient ERK inhibition during 0.5–2 hours is predicted to reduce the epidermal transition and regrowth more than inhibition during 4.5–6 hours under either restricted model. A reversible MEK inhibitor is an initial implementation candidate, with local delivery preferred; it cannot be described as epidermis-specific without direct validation. Vehicle, washout and epidermal/non-epidermal target-engagement measurements are required. If only systemic inhibition is feasible, the result tests ERK necessity somewhere in the animal, not basal-epidermal necessity. Importantly, stage-46 rescue plus stage-40 blockade alone does not establish a timing gate: the matched early-versus-late rescue contrast supplies the discrimination.
reasoning_steps.title: Use the corresponding block as a necessity control, not a sufficient discriminator

reasoning_steps.argument: The primary efficacy endpoint is blinded day-7 regenerated tail length divided by the standardized length removed, capped at one, with death assigned zero and survival separately reported. This measures an operational regrowth outcome, not complete functional regeneration. Record fin, muscle and axial-tissue organization as secondary endpoints. Define D46 = mean(Y_late rescue) − mean(Y_early rescue). A preregistered biologically relevant target is D46 ≥ 0.25 for B_delay or D46 ≤ −0.25 for A_amp, together with a 95% confidence interval excluding zero; these numbers are design thresholds, not estimated effects. Require that the favored rescue also improves over vehicle, since a positive contrast caused only by early-treatment damage is not rescue. Intermediate outcomes are epidermal ERK trajectories, RIC-state induction per basal-epidermal cell, absolute epidermal cell abundance, and subsequent ECM remodeling. Sampling at 0, 0.5, 2, 4.5, 6, 12 and 24 hours brackets the proposed windows; these are new experimental sampling times, not asserted GEO coverage. A single 6-hour state measurement is inadequate because different decay times after the two pulses can mimic different induction.
reasoning_steps.title: Predefine outcomes and numerical decision targets

reasoning_steps.argument: First run a feasibility pilot of 12 animals per efficacy arm, balanced across four clutches, solely to evaluate manipulation and assay validity. The six proposed efficacy arms are stage-46 vehicle, early rescue and late rescue, and stage-40 vehicle, early block and late block. A provisional confirmatory size is 64 animals per arm across eight new clutches. For an independently randomized bounded outcome in [0,1], variance is at most 0.25; the conventional two-group normal approximation gives n ≈ 2(1.96+0.84)^2(0.25)/(0.25)^2 = 62.72 per arm for 80% power against a 0.25 difference at two-sided 0.05. This is a planning approximation, not a guarantee under clutch heterogeneity, discrete outcomes or multiple confirmatory comparisons. Pilot-informed simulation and a frozen analysis plan must precede final enrollment. Randomize individual animals within clutch and developmental stage; avoid treatment-specific shared tanks. If exposure is tank-level, the tank becomes the randomized unit and this animal-level calculation is invalid. Cells and image fields are subsamples, never independent animals.
reasoning_steps.title: Bound sample size and preserve biological units

reasoning_steps.argument: Include wounded vehicle controls, light-only actuator-negative controls, actuator-positive no-light controls, and unamputated treatment controls for toxicity and developmental effects. Standardize amputation plane, staging criteria, feeding, density, temperature and observation time; blind scoring and balance processing batches. Quantify wound closure, epidermal viability and tissue composition so that apparent RIC loss is not merely cell depletion. ERK pulses could rescue through generic growth rather than induction of the proposed epidermal state: rescue without a preceding state-transition change contradicts this specified mediation model. A persistent cell-intrinsic RIC-state block predicts neither early nor late rescue despite target engagement, but that outcome is also compatible with a downstream block or an incorrect tested window. It therefore rejects the bounded two-window rescue hypothesis, not every possible timing mechanism.

A later naturally regained-competence stage, chosen only after confirming X. laevis staging and husbandry behavior, provides an additional independent condition: recovery of early receptivity would support a reversible timing explanation, whereas its absence narrows or contradicts that explanation. Neither this recovery nor an individual predictor is presently demonstrated.

argument_steps.title: Specify a feasible intervention class without claiming an available validated reagent

argument_steps.title: Use the corresponding block as a necessity control, not a sufficient discriminator

argument_steps.title: Predefine outcomes and numerical decision targets

argument_steps.argument: First run a feasibility pilot of 12 animals per efficacy arm, balanced across four clutches, solely to evaluate manipulation and assay validity. argument_steps.title: Counterfactual controls and alternative explanations

argument_steps.argument: Before using GEO data, verify sample identities, pooling, biological replicates, units, processing batches and stage-by-time coverage. reasoning_steps.argument: Let p_early and p_late be nonnegative added ERK-activity pulses supported on the respective windows and having the same positive integral Q. Within stage 46, J_late − J_early = k∫C_46(t)[p_late(t) − p_early(t)]dt, because the untreated trajectory cancels. Thus the sign differs without requiring a difference in total added ERK activity. For nonrectangular receptive windows the contrast measures the pulse-weighted difference in receptivity; its sign is not guaranteed merely by naming a mechanism. A monotone, nonsaturated relationship between transition drive and regrowth transfers this sign to the expected regrowth contrast. Saturation, zero receptivity in both windows or an independent downstream block can erase discrimination.

review.rationale: With C and the untreated trajectory fixed, linearity of the integral gives the stated contrast. Constant c on only one pulse window yields exactly −kcQ or +kcQ. Transfer to regrowth is explicitly conditional on the listed monotone, nonsaturated response assumption; it does not follow from the R and M differential equations alone.

reasoning_steps.argument: A testable candidate is a stage-dependent temporal gate in basal epidermis: an injury-related redox input has different effectiveness depending on when it arrives, rather than competence being determined only by its initial amplitude. Compare locally delivered redox pulses at 0.5–1 versus 3–3.5 hours post-amputation, with achieved local redox exposure matched in a separate calibration pilot. Measure a prespecified per-cell RIC/ECM response score at 6 hours. The directional hypothesis is D=[mean(M_late−M_early) at stage 46]−[mean(M_late−M_early) at stage 40]>0. A timing-invariant inability to enter the RIC state predicts no selective late-pulse rescue. Positive D alone would not exclude metabolic modulation or establish the molecular decoder.

Confirm achieved local redox exposure, cell survival and wound dimensions so dose mismatch or additional injury cannot masquerade as timing. Quantify both basal-cell abundance and within-cell induction; cells are subsamples, not replicates. The terminal 6-hour molecular arm and a separately randomized 7-day regeneration arm test molecular and phenotypic effects, respectively; their animals must not be falsely paired. A later competent stage, selected from independently documented X. laevis phenotyping rather than an assumed cross-species equivalence, is a subsequent test of regained competence.

As a provisional minimum-interest margin, choose D=0.5 pilot-control standard deviations; this is a design choice requiring biological justification, not an effect estimate. Report a clutch-aware 95% interval. An upper bound below 0.5 rejects the prespecified minimum-effect hypothesis; an upper bound at or below zero contradicts its direction; intervals spanning the margin are inconclusive. A positive molecular interaction without an independently estimated regeneration benefit does not establish a regeneration mechanism. For any subsequent animal-level predictor, require a validated nonterminal response assay and actual individual outcome links, then compare against stage-only, stage-plus-RIC/ECM-only and stage-plus-known-signaling baselines on untouched clutch/batch-held-out units. Use identical eligible test animals and report uncertainty in predictive improvement. Do not fit an individual predictor by joining the separate terminal and phenotype arms.

skeptic_output.response:
Cycle 1 establishes a useful conditional identifiability result, not a biological discovery. The constructed distributions have variance 1 and covariance either +1 or −1, so reversing their stage assignments reverses the coupling interaction without changing the observed marginals. The proposed redox-pulse experiment is potentially useful, but its principal contrast has a material, recoverable confound: measuring both treatments at 6 hours gives early and late pulses different response intervals. A positive stage-by-timing interaction could reflect stage-dependent response kinetics or transient score persistence rather than a wound-age-dependent epidermal gate. Matched local exposure does not resolve this. Add matched post-pulse response intervals and time-matched vehicle trajectories before treating the contrast as mechanistically discriminating.

argument_steps.argument: Within stage s, let early response E have values mu_s−1 and mu_s+1 with equal probability. Let the later response M have values nu_s−1 and nu_s+1, also equally often. Model P pairs the same signs within animals, giving Cov(E,M|s)=+1 and regression slope +1. Model N pairs opposite signs, giving covariance and slope −1. Both models have exactly the same early and late marginal distributions, means and variances. These are constructed mathematical values, not expression observations. Assigning P to stage 40 and N to stage 46, or reversing those assignments, produces opposite stage interactions while preserving every stage/time marginal in this example.

argument_steps.title: Construct observationally equivalent coupling mechanisms

argument_steps.argument: Because identical observables can correspond to opposite coupling interactions, no estimator using only unlinked stage/time marginals can generally identify that individual-level interaction. More destructive cross-sectional samples improve marginal precision but do not supply the missing joint distribution. Correlating stage/time averages instead estimates an ecological relationship. Actual longitudinal links, informative interventions or explicit structural restrictions could change identifiability. Paired pools could support a pool-level analysis but would not automatically identify animal-level coupling. The counterexample does not preclude descriptive differential expression or prediction from measurements genuinely available on an individual before its outcome.

review.rationale: Observational equivalence proves nonidentifiability in the unrestricted marginal-only model. Increasing unlinked sample counts does not recover the missing joint distribution. The stated qualifications concerning longitudinal links, structural restrictions and pool-level versus animal-level inference are appropriate.

Compare locally delivered redox pulses at 0.5–1 versus 3–3.5 hours post-amputation, with achieved local redox exposure matched in a separate calibration pilot. Measure a prespecified per-cell RIC/ECM response score at 6 hours. The directional hypothesis is D=[mean(M_late−M_early) at stage 46]−[mean(M_late−M_early) at stage 40]>0. A timing-invariant inability to enter the RIC state predicts no selective late-pulse rescue. A pure tissue-abundance explanation predicts changes in total signal without the corresponding within-basal-cell response. Positive D alone would not exclude metabolic modulation or establish the molecular decoder.

reasoning_steps.argument: The project attributes transient basal-epidermal RIC formation and ECM-remodeling defects to DOI 10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3. It also identifies ROS, immune/developmental signaling, and context-dependent nutritional effects as prior knowledge. These define exclusions from novelty for this project, but the underlying articles have not been inspected here. The provisional ledger is: that 2024 DOI—RIC/ECM prior art according to the supplied description; DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005—reference pointer only, specific experiments and species unverified here; DOI 10.3390/ijms252111597—review pointer only, coverage unverified here; GSE245320 and component accessions—study/data pointers, not independently verified datasets in this session. No search of subsequent work through the supplied November 2026 investigation date has occurred.

reasoning_steps.title: Separate supplied biological background from inspected evidence

reasoning_steps.argument: Let S denote developmental stage, E an animal's early wound-response measurement, and L its later basal-epidermal RIC/ECM activation measurement. An animal-level coupling claim concerns the joint distribution P(E,L|S), for example beta_s = Cov(E,L|S=s)/Var(E|S=s), when the variance is nonzero. Separate destructive collections at early and late times generally estimate only the marginals P(E|S) and P(L|S). Matching stage, batch, or clutch does not turn different animals into repeated measurements.

review.rationale: The proposed regression slope depends on a joint covariance, whereas separate marginal samples do not generally determine that covariance. Matching group labels does not create individual pairing. The slope is meaningful where its requisite moments exist and early-response variance is positive.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the estimand that a temporal-coupling claim needs

reasoning_steps.argument: Take two stage classes and let E equal -1 or +1 with probability one half in each. In model U, set L=E at both stages; both slopes equal +1, so the late-minus-early-stage slope contrast is 0. In model V, set L=E at the first stage and L=-E at the second; the slopes are +1 and -1, giving a contrast of -2. At every stage in both models, E and L separately have the same symmetric two-point distribution, with mean 0 and variance 1. Thus all unpaired marginal observations have identical distributions under U and V, although the proposed coupling interaction differs. Increasing the number of unpaired samples cannot distinguish these models. This is a constructed statistical example, not simulated or observed frog data.

review.rationale: For symmetric ±1 early responses, variance is 1. Setting the later response equal to or opposite the early response gives covariance and slope +1 or −1 while preserving both marginals. The two stated stage contrasts are therefore exactly 0 and −2. This is an analytic construction, not computation or frog data.

reasoning_steps.title: Give an exact nonidentifiability counterexample

reasoning_steps.argument: Adding stage-specific means or positive scale factors to the example preserves the ambiguity: within-stage covariance still depends on the unobserved pairing. A stage-by-time expression contrast can therefore be real and reproducible without identifying within-animal coupling. Likewise, a correlation across a few stage/time group means is an ecological association, not an estimate of beta_s. Predominantly regenerative scRNA-seq can help define candidate cell states, but cannot supply missing refractory observations or reconstruct individual early-to-late pairing without additional validated information.

review.rationale: Stage-specific shifts and positive rescaling leave alternative pairings possible. Group-mean correlations consequently do not recover within-stage individual covariance. Cell-state annotation alone likewise supplies no missing longitudinal identity or refractory sampling.

reasoning_steps.title: Explain why population contrasts do not repair the missing link

reasoning_steps.argument: For GSE245317, GSE245318, GSE245312, and GSE245313, a sample manifest must resolve species, stage at amputation and collection, post-amputation time and its units, tissue boundaries, treatment, assay, animal or pool identity, pool size, library identity, clutch, batch, and regeneration-outcome availability. The supplied stage-40/stage-46 and 0/0.5/6-hour/3-day description is a claim to verify, not a completed factorial design. Technical libraries from one specimen are not additional biological replicates; independently collected pools may be biological sampling units but cannot be presented as individual-animal measurements. Files sharing this study are not independent validation merely because they have different accession numbers.

review.rationale: The listed metadata are appropriate gates for identifying sampling units, design structure, and outcome availability. Technical libraries are not independent biological units, pooled measurements are not individual measurements, and separate accessions within one study do not by themselves establish independent validation.

reasoning_steps.argument: A prospective observational test would measure an early wound-response reporter non-destructively in each animal, then measure a separately validated epidermal RIC/ECM reporter in the same animal, followed by blinded regeneration scoring. Candidate windows are 0–0.5 hours for the early response and approximately 6 hours for the later readout, subject to a separate feasibility pilot establishing reporter kinetics and biological relevance. review.rationale: Validated serial measurements in the same animal would supply the linkage absent from marginal-only sampling. The step correctly treats reporter windows as pilot-dependent and retains animal-level inference and observational-confounding limitations. It establishes a test design, not reporter feasibility or biological coupling.

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed direction is beta_refractory < beta_competent after prespecified adjustment for baseline epidermal abundance, wound size, and batch. Even a persistent negative contrast would not by itself distinguish failed RIC competence from failed signal transmission: that requires a validated perturbation of early signaling plus a downstream bypass/control, with wound closure, toxicity, and reporter effects checked. review.rationale: The negative refractory-versus-competent slope contrast is a directional hypothesis, not a result. reasoning_steps.argument: Let E_i denote an animal's early wound-response measurement, R_i its later epidermal RIC/ECM-transition measurement, and S_i developmental stage. An animal-level coupling estimand is the within-stage slope Cov(E,R|S)/Var(E|S), when the variance is positive. Measurements from different animals at different times estimate marginal distributions, not this joint distribution. Whether the actual GEO samples provide animal linkage, independent animals, pools, or only technical/library replication remains unverified. Pool-level results must not be represented as animal-level prediction.

review.rationale: Cov(E,R|S)/Var(E|S) is a defined within-stage linear-projection slope when the relevant moments exist and variance is positive. Unlinked sampling supplies marginals rather than animal correspondence. The step explicitly leaves the GEO sampling premise unverified.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the estimand and the unresolved sampling prerequisite

reasoning_steps.argument: Within one stage, let U be uniform on [0,1]. Model I assigns E=U and R=U; Model II assigns E=U and R=1−U. Both models give exactly the same uniform marginal distributions for E and R. However, Var(E)=1/12, while Cov(E,R)=1/12 in Model I and −1/12 in Model II; the coupling slopes are therefore +1 and −1. Independently sampled early and late animals have identical observable distributions under these two models. Thus no analysis of those unlinked measurements alone can distinguish even the sign of individual coupling. Additional unlinked time points do not supply the missing individual correspondence without extra, testable structural assumptions. This construction is an identifiability proof, not a biological model of tadpole expression.

review.rationale: For uniform U, Var(U)=1/12 and Cov(U,1−U)=−1/12. Both constructions have identical early and late marginals, hence identical observable laws under independent unlinked sampling, while their slopes differ. This establishes a general nonidentifiability counterexample, not impossibility under every additional structural model.

reasoning_steps.title: Prove nonidentifiability from unlinked marginals

reasoning_steps.argument: For two stages coded S=0 or 1, suppose every late sample receives its stage's early mean, E=e0+(e1−e0)S. Then S·E=e1S. Consequently, a regression containing an intercept, stage, assigned early mean and stage×early-mean has rank at most two. Its proposed interaction is not separately identifiable. More biological replicates at the late time improve precision of stage means but do not repair this rank deficiency. Independent early cohorts can estimate population response trajectories; those trajectories must not be relabeled as matched individual predictors.

review.rationale: With binary S, the assigned E lies in the span of the intercept and S, and SE=e1S. Thus all specified columns lie in a two-dimensional span regardless of replicate count. Population trajectory estimation remains distinct from individual coupling.

reasoning_steps.title: Identify a second failure mode: stage means masquerading as interactions

reasoning_steps.argument: For prospective X. laevis experiments, measure basal-epidermal peroxide dynamics non-destructively in each animal. Define B as the baseline-adjusted reporter area under the curve over 0–0.5 hours and P as the mean baseline-adjusted response over 0.5–6 hours. Define R as a prespecified, per-animal RIC/ECM-transition score at 24 hours, using modules and identity criteria fixed after inspecting the reference study rather than selected for a stage contrast. The candidate rule is that, among animals with adequate B, larger P predicts smaller R; experimentally reducing P without reducing B should increase R. Stage 46 is predicted to show excess persistence rather than merely a smaller initial response. A later independently verified competent stage should regain a short response tail. These directions are predictions, including the proposed recovery pattern, not observations. An adequate-B range must be calibrated and frozen before the confirmatory experiment; no threshold is presently established.

review.objection: P is the 0.5–6-hour integral divided by 5.5 hours. It is a burden measure, not a shape-specific persistence measure. Define a separate temporal-shape estimand before treating this as a discriminating persistence rule.
review.rationale: The direction, time window and tissue are specified as predictions rather than observations, but the operational definition does not isolate temporal persistence.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify the candidate temporal rule

reasoning_steps.argument: After a separate feasibility pilot, randomize stage-40 and stage-46 animals within clutch to temporally controlled basal-epidermal peroxide removal during 0.5–6 hours or a matched inactive control. Inducible catalase is a candidate implementation, not an available or validated reagent here. Verify that the intervention lowers P while preserving B, wound closure and viability; include reporter pH controls and an orthogonal peroxide assay. Use 24 animals per stage×treatment cell, balanced across four clutches: 96 animals for the primary molecular endpoint. Record E non-destructively and then measure R in the same animals. Cell counts are subsamples; the animal is the inferential unit. A reciprocal competent-stage peroxide-persistence arm and a 6–12-hour timing control are required before a mechanistic conclusion. To distinguish persistence from total oxidant burden, additionally compare short-tail and long-tail schedules matched on measured 0.5–6-hour reporter integral and initial B; equal nominal reagent dose is not adequate matching. If that matching cannot be achieved, the persistence-versus-total-dose interpretation remains unresolved.

review.objection: Integral-matched schedules necessarily have equal P, so this contrast does not test the current P-based mechanism. The reciprocal, timing and shape-control arms also need an explicit allocation or staged budget to make the entire experiment bounded.
review.rationale: Within-clutch randomization, animal-level inference, target-engagement checks and reporter controls are appropriate design components. The stated 96 animals cover only the primary two-stage, two-treatment comparison.

reasoning_steps.title: Design the bounded discriminating experiment

reasoning_steps.argument: The primary estimand is the randomized treatment effect on R within stage 46, with clutch blocking and a treatment×stage contrast reported separately. Define a minimum biologically interesting rescue as +0.5 control-standard-deviation units of R, using an independent pilot to freeze the scaling. This is a proposed decision threshold, not an effect estimate. Report effect sizes and 95% confidence intervals. An upper confidence limit below +0.5 SD would reject a rescue of that prespecified size, not every smaller gate effect; a precise nonpositive effect after verified target engagement would contradict the predicted direction. Failure to preserve B or obtain target engagement makes the experiment inconclusive rather than a negative mechanism test. In paired prospective observations compare stage-only, initial-response-only, known-signaling-module, and composition-adjusted models before adding P and its interaction with B. Gene sets, transformations and regularization must be frozen before evaluation, with entire clutches held out and preprocessing confined to training data. Permuting P within stage and clutch is a negative-control analysis. Wide intervals or unstable held-out improvement trigger an unresolved result, not a claim of predictive success. The proposed sample size is a finite budget, not a power guarantee.

review.objection: Explicitly include the required RIC/ECM-only baseline and define what each model predicts and when each predictor is measured. A concurrent RIC/ECM score cannot serve as a leakage-free baseline for predicting that same score. Composition-adjusted analysis is useful but does not replace the missing baseline.
review.rationale: The distinction between a +0.5-SD target and an observed effect is sound, as are the restricted interpretation of an upper confidence bound, target-engagement requirement and clutch-level holdout. Predictive evaluation remains incompletely specified.

reasoning_steps.title: Predefine analysis, numerical targets and falsification

reasoning_steps.argument: A randomized late-redox rescue with preserved initial signaling would argue against a strictly stage-fixed, nonresponsive epidermal-transition failure, although it would not exclude other upstream causes or downstream redox effects. Reciprocal suppression and the integral-matched timing contrast are needed to support a temporal gate rather than generic ROS dependence. Measure RIC fraction, absolute basal-epidermal cell abundance and within-cell transition markers separately so that a change in cell mixture is not mistaken for altered state. A separately randomized regeneration cohort must test later anatomical recovery with blinded scoring; animals sacrificed for the 24-hour molecular endpoint cannot also supply later regrowth outcomes. A molecular rescue without functional regeneration does not establish regeneration competence. Nutritional state, clutch, staging, amputation position and husbandry require blocking or standardization. Restored competence at a later stage requires its own verified baseline and independent test, not extrapolation from stages 40 and 46.

review.rationale: A selective randomized molecular rescue would challenge a strictly nonresponsive stage-fixed failure, but would not by itself identify the full upstream mechanism. Separating state from abundance, molecular from functional outcomes, and stage-40/46 effects from later recovery is logically necessary. This accepts the limited interpretation and required controls, not the adequacy of the presently defined timing contrast.

DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005 and review DOI 10.3390/ijms252111597 are additional uninspected prior-art leads; no more specific contents are attributed to them. Whether late peroxide resolution, this conditional rule, or its rescue experiment has already been reported is unknown, including later work through the investigation date. The contribution is therefore a standard statistical identifiability argument plus a specific proposed experiment. Biological novelty, empirical generality and practical efficacy are not assessed. Exit status is NEGATIVE/UNRESOLVED empirically, with an unverified candidate hypothesis retained for testing.

review.rationale: The step accurately treats supplied references as uninspected leads, avoids asserting independent replication from component series, and labels the empirical result unresolved. No supplied evidence supports a stronger novelty or efficacy conclusion.

strategy_findings.skeptic_response:
Cycle 1 establishes a useful conditional identifiability result, not a biological discovery. The uniform-variable construction correctly shows that unlinked early and late measurements cannot generally determine even the sign of animal-level coupling. The stage-mean interaction is also exactly rank-deficient as specified. Neither result establishes how the GEO samples were collected; accession-level application remains conditional on an unverified sampling audit.

The proposed experiment has a material, recoverable inconsistency: P is the mean reporter response over 0.5–6 hours, so P equals the reporter integral over that interval divided by 5.5 hours. Matching that integral necessarily matches P. Consequently, the proposed integral-matched short-tail/long-tail contrast cannot distinguish effects through P as currently defined. A timing-dependent difference under matched P would instead show that P is an insufficient description of the proposed gate. Separate total burden from temporal shape before claiming to discriminate persistence from generic ROS dependence.

A feasible next conceptual step is to define a temporal-shape quantity, such as the fraction of the 0.5–6-hour integral occurring during 3–6 hours, with a prespecified positive-integral eligibility rule. Compare profiles matched on initial response and total integral but differing in this late fraction. State separately what the burden-reduction experiment and the matched-shape experiment test. This is a proposed repair, not evidence that such profiles or interventions are biologically achievable.

The supplied proposal appropriately avoids invented expression values, effect estimates, successful executions, novelty claims and cross-species transfers. The +0.5-SD value is a decision threshold, not a measured effect. Novelty, empirical generality and efficacy remain unassessed. No external evidence or computation is supplied. The operational failures do not refute the hypothesis; replacing an unavailable computation with an analytical argument is operational recovery, not empirical progress.
strategy_findings.strategy_title: Find a novel temporal coupling, not another marker

strategy_findings.claim: An exact illustrative construction establishes that identical marginal injury and ECM activity can conceal different spatial alignment. Spatial alignment between early basal-epidermal injury signaling and later local ECM activity is a testable candidate predictor, not an established biological mechanism or a demonstrated novel association.

reasoning_steps.argument: The supplied project description attributes basal-epidermal RIC origins and ECM-remodeling defects to doi:10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3; these are treated as already-known exclusions, not new findings. It identifies GSE245320, bulk components GSE245317/GSE245318, scRNA GSE245312, and spatial GSE245313 as a shared-study resource. Actual sample coverage, biological units, pooling, spatial resolution, and availability have not been verified. The supplied doi:10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005 and review doi:10.3390/ijms252111597 are ledger entries awaiting inspection, not sources whose detailed conclusions I have checked. Subsequent literature through the investigation date, 2026-11-01, is also unchecked. Therefore spatial coupling may already have prior art, and no novelty priority is claimed.

review.objection: This entry is designated an assumption, while claim_is_conditional is false. It cannot be accepted as an established premise. Its accession descriptions and prior-art attributions remain background awaiting inspection.
review.rationale: The evidence boundary is appropriately disclosed, and the project-supplied references are correctly treated as provisional rather than inspected sources.

reasoning_steps.title: Evidence boundary and provisional prior-art ledger

reasoning_steps.argument: Consider four equally weighted, registered wound positions. Let early basal injury activity be I=(1,1,0,0). Two possible later local ECM-activity fields are M_A=(1,1,0,0) and M_B=(0,0,1,1). Both have identical activity totals, identical numbers of active positions, and mean activity 1/2. Define Q_raw=mean(I*M)-mean(I)mean(M). Then Q_raw(A)=2/4-1/4=1/4, whereas Q_raw(B)=0-1/4=-1/4. Thus the marginal measurements are identical but spatial coupling differs by 1/2. This exact illustrative construction proves non-identification by those marginals; it neither demonstrates such arrangements in tadpoles nor shows that the arrangements affect regeneration.

review.rationale: Direct arithmetic gives mean(I)=mean(M)=1/2, mean(I*M_A)=1/2, and mean(I*M_B)=0, hence covariances 1/4 and -1/4. The conclusion is correctly restricted to non-identification by the specified marginals.

reasoning_steps.title: Why abundance cannot identify the proposed interaction

reasoning_steps.argument: For each animal, segment basal epidermal regions j in a preregistered wound region and track their positions from 0.5 to 6 hours. Let I_j be validated injury-response reporter activity at 0.5 hours. Let M_j be ECM-cleavage activity within one median basal-cell diameter beneath the tracked region at 6 hours. Use equal-area weights and define T=mean_j(I_j*M_j). Define Q=T-E_null(T), where the null reassigns injury measurements among comparable positions within preregistered wound-distance and anatomical strata, preserving the observed marginal fields, cell counts, and geometry. Finite-permutation precision must be reported. This null tests alignment beyond those chosen constraints, not beyond every possible anatomical confound. Injury and ECM probes must be selected and locked before examining regeneration outcomes; neither reporter availability nor specificity is established here.

review.objection: Acceptance concerns the definition only. Biological inference still requires a defensible exchangeability model and sensitivity to spatial autocorrelation, registration error, and stratum choice.
review.rationale: T minus its specified null expectation is a coherent definition of excess alignment. The text explicitly limits interpretation to the chosen constraints and does not claim reporter validity or control of all anatomy.

reasoning_steps.title: Operational definition of the candidate predictor

reasoning_steps.argument: The candidate predicts a positive relationship between Q and subsequent RIC-state induction per eligible basal cell, followed by improved regeneration, conditional on stage, basal-cell abundance, mean injury activity, total ECM activity, and wound closure. The proposed refractory-stage defect is reduced alignment, not necessarily reduced totals. A pure abundance explanation predicts no additional association once cell composition is accounted for. Generalized healing predicts that wound closure, viability, or nonspecific wound-associated patterns explain the association. A metabolic or anatomical common cause could still produce both alignment and regeneration; an observational Q association would not establish causality. If alignment explains the developmental switch, it should also return at an independently confirmed later competent stage, not merely separate stages 40 and 46.

review.objection: Neither the positive association nor its developmental loss-and-return pattern follows from the illustrative construction. They require biological observations; adjustment alone cannot establish a coupling defect.
review.rationale: The directional hypothesis, eligible-cell denominator, nuisance variables, later-stage requirement, and common-cause alternative are clearly identified.

reasoning_steps.title: Biological prediction and competing explanations

reasoning_steps.argument: The bounded archival task is to inspect sample tables, library provenance, stage/time labels, animal or pool identifiers, spatial capture units, available images, and expression matrices before selecting any contrast. GSE245312 could supply reference cell labels and candidate marker panels, while GSE245313 could establish whether relevant signals are anatomically separable at its actual resolution. Neither role is guaranteed by accession alone. If spots contain mixed cells, co-detection does not establish apposition or within-cell induction. Reference-based deconvolution must carry uncertainty and be checked against histology. Predominantly regenerating scRNA samples cannot establish refractory-stage cell states; missing reference states may be misassigned to abundance changes. Unpaired destructive time points cannot estimate an individual animal's longitudinal Q. Cells, spots, and sections remain nested observations, not biological replicates; the shared study is not independent confirmation.

review.rationale: The stated identifiability limits follow: unlinked destructive samples cannot yield individual longitudinal Q, mixed spots cannot establish apposition, and cells or sections do not independently replicate animals. Suggested atlas uses are explicitly contingent on an audit.

reasoning_steps.title: What the public atlas can and cannot test

reasoning_steps.argument: After assay validation, preregister a capped study of 240 previously unseen X. laevis animals from 12 clutches, balanced as feasible across stages 40, 46, and a later stage first confirmed to regain competence. Allocate eight whole clutches to model development and four to locked evaluation; randomize imaging order and experimental batches within stage and blind outcome scoring. Live measurements at 0.5 and 6 hours must leave animals available for a prespecified day-7 regeneration outcome. Separate destructive cohorts can measure later RIC induction per basal cell but cannot substitute for individual predictor-outcome linkage. Compare stage-only, RIC/ECM-only, known-signaling-module, and combined nuisance baselines with the same combined model plus one Q term; freeze all feature selection and scaling in development data. Baseline assays must be feasible and prespecified, not omitted after seeing results. Proposed computational support requires positive held-out log-loss improvement with a clutch-level 95% interval excluding zero and an adjusted Q association in the predicted direction. The target odds ratio is 1.5 per SD; an upper confidence limit below 1.5 would rule out that prespecified useful effect, not every possible effect. No effect, uncertainty interval, power, or predictive gain has been measured.

review.objection: The same-animal RIC/ECM baseline remains unspecified, and the interval procedure and precision attainable with four evaluation clutches are not established. The conditional odds-ratio estimand also needs to be distinguished from held-out predictive improvement.
review.rationale: Whole-clutch evaluation, training-only scaling, simple baselines, and separation of a target odds ratio from an estimate are appropriate design choices.

reasoning_steps.title: Prospective biological test and numerical decision rules

reasoning_steps.argument: Compare the true registered field with geometry-constrained spatial reassignments and a prespecified distant-tissue alignment control. Measure wound closure, survival, cell density, and reporter-independent ECM-probe background. Test sensitivity to neighborhood radii of 0.5, 1, and 2 basal-cell diameters without selecting the best radius post hoc. A causal follow-up would randomize spatially localized ECM activation near early injury-high versus injury-low regions, matching total dose and including sham illumination or delivery controls. The prediction is greater RIC induction and regeneration for aligned activation at matched abundance and total activity. This counterfactual is informative only if a safe, selective local manipulation can be validated; changing dose, cell viability, or overall wound closure would make the comparison non-discriminating. Simply rescuing ECM activity everywhere would not isolate the spatial rule.

review.objection: This accepts the experimental contrast, not manipulation feasibility or the predicted biological result.
review.rationale: As a prospective design, randomized aligned versus misaligned local activation at matched total activity can distinguish a spatial rule from a total-dose explanation. The text correctly makes informativeness contingent on selective manipulation and comparable viability and healing.

reasoning_steps.title: Negative controls and a mechanistic counterfactual

reasoning_steps.argument: Reject the proposed useful predictor if a sufficiently precise independent test excludes the prespecified positive effect, if geometry-matched scrambled fields predict equally well, or if cell abundance and healing fully account for its added predictive value. Failure to obtain precise estimates is inconclusive, not falsification. Stop the archival arm if relevant spatial contrasts or biological-unit metadata are absent; report the gap rather than manufacture matched samples. Stop claims of within-stage prediction if outcomes do not vary sufficiently within stage, and stop causal claims unless the spatial counterfactual is feasible and discriminating. With only four held-out clutches, uncertainty may remain large; the animal cap is not a power calculation, and simulation-based planning is required before animal work. The current contribution is a testable hypothesis plus a standard identifiability argument. Material novelty, biological generality, predictive usefulness, and explanation of the loss-and-return switch remain unresolved.

review.objection: The stopping rules are not yet operational for scrambled-field equivalence or complete explanation by nuisance baselines. Similar point estimates alone do not reject a useful predictor; prespecified precision or equivalence criteria are needed.
review.rationale: The separation of inconclusive precision from falsification and the prohibition on unsupported causal claims are sound.

reasoning_steps.title: Falsification, stopping, and contribution level

strategy_findings.skeptic_response: Cycle 1 supplies a useful spatial-coupling hypothesis and a correct analytical demonstration that marginal activity summaries cannot identify spatial alignment. It does not establish that alignment changes in tadpoles, predicts regeneration, or is previously unreported. The biological objective remains unresolved. Before biological testing, the proposal needs an explicitly calibrated spatial null, feasible same-animal baseline measurements, and a precision plan. The recorded cancellations and budget denials are operational history, not biological evidence; making no execution request is appropriate given the unavailable runtimes.
strategy_findings.strategy_title: Test a spatial or cell-composition alternative

reasoning_steps.argument: The project supplies the following provisional ledger: DOI 10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3 is described as establishing basal-epidermal RIC origins and ECM-remodeling defects; those features are therefore not claimed as novel. DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005 and review DOI 10.3390/ijms252111597 are relevant starting references, but their detailed contents have not been inspected. GSE245320 and its component accessions are candidate observational resources, not independent replications. The proposed contribution is specifically a stage-dependent pulse-timing response at matched signal exposure, not identification of ERK, RICs or ECM as regeneration-related. Originality and later-publication coverage remain unassessed.

review.rationale: The boundary matches the project-supplied description and explicitly distinguishes that description from inspected literature. It does not claim verified novelty or independent replication.

reasoning_steps.title: Scope and prior-art boundary

reasoning_steps.argument: Let E_s(t) denote measured basal-epidermal ERK activity at stage s, C_s(t) denote receptivity to enter the transient regenerative epidermal state, and J_s = k∫E_s(t)C_s(t)dt denote cumulative transition drive, with k > 0. Downstream state occupancy R and remodeling M can be represented by dR/dt = kEC − δ_R R and dM/dt = aR − δ_M M. Model A_amp attributes stage-46 failure to insufficient early E, with C concentrated in the early window at both stages. Model B_delay retains early receptivity at stage 40 but places stage-46 receptivity in the late window. These are deliberately restricted alternatives; broad 'failure to induce RICs' includes both and cannot itself be distinguished by this experiment.

review.rationale: The equations define coherent restricted candidate models. They are not inferred from data, and the argument correctly recognizes that broad RIC-induction failure contains both alternatives.

reasoning_steps.title: Define the two restricted competing mechanisms

reasoning_steps.argument: Let p_early and p_late be nonnegative added ERK-activity pulses supported on the respective windows and having the same positive integral Q. Within stage 46, J_late − J_early = k∫C_46(t)[p_late(t) − p_early(t)]dt, because the untreated trajectory cancels. In the idealized A_amp model, C_46 equals c > 0 in the early window and zero in the late window, so the contrast is −kcQ. In B_delay the supports are reversed, giving +kcQ. Thus the sign differs without requiring a difference in total added ERK activity. For nonrectangular receptive windows the contrast measures the pulse-weighted difference in receptivity; its sign is not guaranteed merely by naming a mechanism. A monotone, nonsaturated relationship between transition drive and regrowth transfers this sign to the expected regrowth contrast. Saturation, zero receptivity in both windows or an independent downstream block can erase discrimination.

review.rationale: With C and the untreated trajectory fixed, linearity of the integral gives the stated contrast. Constant c on only one pulse window yields exactly −kcQ or +kcQ. Transfer to regrowth is explicitly conditional on the listed monotone, nonsaturated response assumption; it does not follow from the R and M differential equations alone.

reasoning_steps.title: Derive the pulse-timing discrimination

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed stage-46 rescue uses a light-gated RAF/ERK actuator expressed specifically in basal epidermis, comparing early versus late activation. A separate validation cohort must establish expression specificity, ERK activation kinetics, reversibility and noninjurious illumination. Actuator availability and efficacy in these cells are unverified. Measured epidermal ERK trajectories, rather than light duration, define exposure; pulse amplitude and integral should be matched within a preregistered tolerance, provisionally 10%. If endogenous early activity is already near saturation, a larger early light dose is not an adequate matched-exposure control. Failure to achieve comparable perturbations makes the biological contrast uninterpretable and stops the efficacy experiment.

review.rationale: This is a feasibility-gated intervention proposal, not an assertion that a validated X. laevis reagent exists. Measuring activity rather than equating illumination durations appropriately addresses stage-dependent actuator response.

reasoning_steps.title: Specify a feasible intervention class without claiming an available validated reagent

reasoning_steps.argument: At stage 40, transient ERK inhibition during 0.5–2 hours is predicted to reduce the epidermal transition and regrowth more than inhibition during 4.5–6 hours under either restricted model. A reversible MEK inhibitor is an initial implementation candidate, with local delivery preferred; it cannot be described as epidermis-specific without direct validation. Vehicle, washout and epidermal/non-epidermal target-engagement measurements are required. If only systemic inhibition is feasible, the result tests ERK necessity somewhere in the animal, not basal-epidermal necessity. Importantly, stage-46 rescue plus stage-40 blockade alone does not establish a timing gate: the matched early-versus-late rescue contrast supplies the discrimination.

review.rationale: Under early-supported stage-40 receptivity, suppressing relevant early activity reduces cumulative transition drive whereas late suppression does not. The proposal correctly limits systemic inhibition to organism-level necessity and identifies the rescue timing contrast as the discriminator. These remain conditional predictions, not demonstrated necessity.

reasoning_steps.title: Use the corresponding block as a necessity control, not a sufficient discriminator

reasoning_steps.argument: The primary efficacy endpoint is blinded day-7 regenerated tail length divided by the standardized length removed, capped at one, with death assigned zero and survival separately reported. This measures an operational regrowth outcome, not complete functional regeneration. Record fin, muscle and axial-tissue organization as secondary endpoints. Define D46 = mean(Y_late rescue) − mean(Y_early rescue). A preregistered biologically relevant target is D46 ≥ 0.25 for B_delay or D46 ≤ −0.25 for A_amp, together with a 95% confidence interval excluding zero; these numbers are design thresholds, not estimated effects. Require that the favored rescue also improves over vehicle, since a positive contrast caused only by early-treatment damage is not rescue. Intermediate outcomes are epidermal ERK trajectories, RIC-state induction per basal-epidermal cell, absolute epidermal cell abundance, and subsequent ECM remodeling. Sampling at 0, 0.5, 2, 4.5, 6, 12 and 24 hours brackets the proposed windows; these are new experimental sampling times, not asserted GEO coverage. A single 6-hour state measurement is inadequate because different decay times after the two pulses can mimic different induction.

review.objection: The molecular transition assay and its sensitivity remain an implementation obligation; no numerical effect or uncertainty has been measured.
review.rationale: The bounded regrowth endpoint and 0.25 contrast are explicitly prospective choices, consistent with the listed design-choice assumption. Requiring improvement over vehicle prevents a harmful early treatment from being mislabeled as late rescue. Serial measurements appropriately recognize unequal time since pulse.

reasoning_steps.title: Predefine outcomes and numerical decision targets

reasoning_steps.argument: First run a feasibility pilot of 12 animals per efficacy arm, balanced across four clutches, solely to evaluate manipulation and assay validity. The six proposed efficacy arms are stage-46 vehicle, early rescue and late rescue, and stage-40 vehicle, early block and late block. A provisional confirmatory size is 64 animals per arm across eight new clutches. For an independently randomized bounded outcome in [0,1], variance is at most 0.25; the conventional two-group normal approximation gives n ≈ 2(1.96+0.84)^2(0.25)/(0.25)^2 = 62.72 per arm for 80% power against a 0.25 difference at two-sided 0.05. This is a planning approximation, not a guarantee under clutch heterogeneity, discrete outcomes or multiple confirmatory comparisons. Pilot-informed simulation and a frozen analysis plan must precede final enrollment. Randomize individual animals within clutch and developmental stage; avoid treatment-specific shared tanks. If exposure is tank-level, the tank becomes the randomized unit and this animal-level calculation is invalid. Cells and image fields are subsamples, never independent animals.

review.rationale: The stated normal-approximation arithmetic gives 62.72 animals per group using variance 0.25 and a 0.25 difference. The proposal explicitly limits this calculation to independent units, flags clustering and multiplicity, and does not present it as a completed power analysis.

reasoning_steps.title: Bound sample size and preserve biological units

reasoning_steps.argument: Include wounded vehicle controls, light-only actuator-negative controls, actuator-positive no-light controls, and unamputated treatment controls for toxicity and developmental effects. Standardize amputation plane, staging criteria, feeding, density, temperature and observation time; blind scoring and balance processing batches. Quantify wound closure, epidermal viability and tissue composition so that apparent RIC loss is not merely cell depletion. ERK pulses could rescue through generic growth rather than induction of the proposed epidermal state: rescue without a preceding state-transition change contradicts this specified mediation model. A persistent cell-intrinsic RIC-state block predicts neither early nor late rescue despite target engagement, but that outcome is also compatible with a downstream block or an incorrect tested window. It therefore rejects the bounded two-window rescue hypothesis, not every possible timing mechanism.

review.objection: No detected transition is not equivalent to no transition. Define the state, assay detection limits and sampling coverage before treating rescue without a detected state change as a contradiction.
review.rationale: The controls and distinction between a failed two-window test and rejection of all timing mechanisms are appropriate. However, the proposed mediation falsifier requires an adequately sensitive and temporally complete state assay that has not yet been specified.

reasoning_steps.title: Counterfactual controls and alternative explanations

reasoning_steps.argument: Before using GEO data, verify sample identities, pooling, biological replicates, units, processing batches and stage-by-time coverage. Cross-sectional bulk samples cannot establish an individual animal's early-to-late coupling, and predominantly regenerating scRNA-seq cannot supply missing matched refractory trajectories. In new specimens, a nonlethal validated ERK/state reporter would permit within-animal temporal measurements followed by day-7 scoring; otherwise molecular companion cohorts support only group-level mediation. Any predictive analysis must compare stage-only, RIC/ECM-only and known-signaling baselines with the timing interaction on held-out clutches, using animal-level uncertainty. A later naturally regained-competence stage, chosen only after confirming X. laevis staging and husbandry behavior, provides an additional independent condition: recovery of early receptivity would support a reversible timing explanation, whereas its absence narrows or contradicts that explanation. Neither this recovery nor an individual predictor is presently demonstrated.

review.rationale: The restrictions on cross-sectional inference, cell pseudoreplication and held-out-clutch prediction are sound. The later-stage test is explicitly prospective. Restoration of early receptivity would support the narrower recovery model, while other restoration-of-overlap mechanisms would remain possible.

reasoning_steps.title: Observational linkage, individual prediction and independent validation

reasoning_steps.argument: Proceed only with institutional animal-care approval, trained Xenopus personnel, validated anesthesia and analgesia where required, humane endpoints, light/drug safety procedures and a reduction-oriented pilot. Stop before efficacy testing if the actuator or inhibitor cannot produce the intended reversible activity trajectory, or if toxicity, wound closure or general development differs meaningfully from controls. Treat excess mortality of 10 percentage points as a provisional safety stop requiring veterinary review, not as an acceptable harm allowance. After a technically valid test, failure of either pulse to improve stage-46 regrowth rules out the tested rescue protocol; failure of stage-40 early blockade to alter the transition weakens the ERK-specific premise. No model is selected if confidence intervals remain compatible with both timing orders. Confirm any favorable result in previously unseen clutches using an orthogonal perturbation before claiming a mechanism.

review.objection: Replace 'failure of either pulse to improve rules out the tested rescue protocol' with a precision-based rule. A technically valid but imprecise null result must remain inconclusive; exclusion should concern a prespecified meaningful effect, not every possible benefit.
review.rationale: Ethical approval, technical validation, safety review and orthogonal confirmation are appropriate gates. The stated efficacy stop rule nevertheless conflates failure to demonstrate improvement with evidence excluding improvement.

reasoning_steps.title: Stop conditions and ethical boundary

strategy_findings.skeptic_response: Cycle 1 supplies a useful conditional discrimination experiment, not an explanation established in X. laevis. The opposite signs of the proposed transition-drive contrast follow for the two explicitly restricted receptivity models. Importantly, this does not distinguish every amplitude defect from every timing defect, and the assumed relationship between cumulative transition drive and regrowth remains untested. The proposal correctly treats novelty, actuator feasibility, GEO coverage and all numerical effects as unresolved. Its principal recoverable inference problem is that failure to observe rescue is not sufficient to rule out the tested protocol without adequate precision and verified target engagement. State-transition readouts also need an operational definition and sensitivity criterion before their apparent absence can contradict mediation. No computation or experiment occurred; earlier cancellations and budget failures provide no biological evidence.

strategy_findings.claim: Conditional on: For the identifiability claim, early and late measurements are from different biological units without an observed link between them; For the identifiability claim, available information consists of stage/time marginal distributions, without additional justified restrictions identifying their joint distribution. Conditional on observing only unlinked stage/time marginal distributions, without additional identifying restrictions, the animal-level early-to-late coupling interaction is not generally identifiable. Whether those conditions describe the GEO data is unknown. The redox timing-gate mechanism remains an unconfirmed candidate with unassessed novelty.

objections: Material and recoverable: the fixed 6-hour endpoint confounds pulse timing with elapsed time since treatment. Stage-dependent response kinetics can produce the proposed interaction without the claimed wound-age-dependent gate.

Material and recoverable: neither accession structure nor prior reporting of the timing interaction has been inspected. The mathematical limitation cannot yet be attributed to the actual GEO samples, and novelty cannot be claimed.

Material and recoverable: no independent molecular or regeneration measurements support the candidate, and no verified later-competent X. laevis condition tests regained competence. These are missing evidence, not refutations.
open_obligations: Acquire original GEO sample metadata and files; verify species, exact stages/times, independent animals versus pools, pairing, batches, replicate counts, outcome labels and assay availability before analysis. If only unlinked snapshots exist, stop the animal-level temporal-coupling analysis.

Inspect the cited original papers and later literature through the investigation date; record exact evidence for or against prior reporting of the pulse-timing interaction. If already established, abandon its novelty claim.

problem:
Why can Xenopus laevis tadpoles regrow a tail at some stages, temporarily lose much of that ability, and later regain it? Investigate a specific, testable mechanism for this developmental switch; regeneration competence varies between animals.

The goal is to discover and test a previously unreported, mechanistically discriminating predictor of this switch, not to summarize known regenerative pathways or to claim all embryonic regeneration explained.

KNOWN, NOT NOVEL. A 2024 Genome Biology study identified transient regeneration-initiating cells (RICs) originating from basal epidermal cells and extracellular-matrix remodeling defects associated with regeneration failure. Other work links ROS, inflammatory and developmental signals to regeneration, and studies in X. tropicalis implicate nutritional state in stage-dependent competence. Merely identifying RICs, Wnt/BMP/FGF/ROS, ECM remodeling, or the existence of a refractory stage does NOT satisfy this project. Cross-species stage behavior is context-dependent and publications are not fully consistent; do not conflate X. tropicalis and X. laevis.

OBSERVATIONAL START. Reanalyze publicly available X. laevis regeneration/refractory transcriptomic evidence from GEO GSE245320 and its component series (bulk RNA-seq GSE245317/GSE245318, scRNA-seq GSE245312, spatial GSE245313). In the published stage-40 versus stage-46 comparison, bulk assays include 0, 0.5, 6 hours post-amputation and 3 days; verify actual samples, replicates, units and availability before analysis. scRNA-seq predominantly characterizes regenerating animals, not matched single-cell snapshots across both conditions. These datasets share a study and are NOT independent biological replications. Check later published work through the investigation date and build a cited prior-art ledger.

HYPOTHESIS SPACE. Competing mechanisms include (A) failure to induce the transient epidermal RIC/ECM-remodeling transition, (B) a stage-specific failure to couple early injury signaling to a later regenerative transcriptional program, (C) metabolic or tissue-composition gating, and (D) analytical or developmental-stage confounding. Prioritize one previously unreported *interaction, conditional dependency, or quantitative transition rule* that distinguishes at least two mechanisms, with a measurable direction, timing, tissue/cell type and uncertainty. A possible candidate is a temporal coupling between early wound-response intensity and subsequent RIC/ECM activation that differs by developmental stage; this is a hypothesis to test, not a finding.

RESEARCH METHOD. Predefine biological replicate as the unit of inference; guard against pseudoreplication (cells from the same animal/library), batch confounding, developmental-stage differences, multiple testing, cell-composition artifacts and publication reuse. Fit simple baselines (stage-only, RIC/ECM-only and known signaling modules) before proposing complexity. Quantify uncertainty and require an alternative explanation and counterfactual control. Do not invent gene-expression values, available outcome labels, intervention results, P values or accession coverage. Predictions based solely on stage class labels must not be marketed as predicting animal-level regeneration.

EXIT CRITERIA. Scientific success requires: (1) traceable evidence that the central claim is not simply already established; (2) a specified novel mechanistic prediction, including what experiment, perturbation or independent observations would falsify it; (3) a numerical effect/direction and uncertainty with appropriate baselines and negative controls; and (4) independent biological evidence on previously unseen specimens/conditions supporting the prediction. Independent replication or perturbation confirmation is required before claiming a new biological mechanism. A lower-tier COMPUTATIONAL RESULT can be reported if a previously unreported reproducible association or predictive rule outperforms preregistered known-mechanism baselines on held-out biological units with uncertainty; label it computational, exploratory and not causal. A NOVEL HYPOTHESIS can be reported with a discriminating experiment and evidence synthesis but without confirmation; do not present it as a validated scientific discovery. Otherwise exit NEGATIVE/UNRESOLVED with exact failed hypotheses, missing data and next experiment. Each strategy must deliver a bounded test and stop conditions. Avoid claiming 'solved regeneration' from any single dataset.

REFERENCES/STARTING DATA. https://doi.org/10.1186/s13059-024-03396-3 ; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/query/acc.cgi?acc=GSE245320 ; https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005; review https://doi.org/10.3390/ijms252111597 .

reasoning_steps.argument: Take two stage classes and let E equal -1 or +1 with probability one half in each. In model U, set L=E at both stages; both slopes equal +1, so the late-minus-early-stage slope contrast is 0. In model V, set L=E at the first stage and L=-E at the second; the slopes are +1 and -1, giving a contrast of -2. At every stage in both models, E and L separately have the same symmetric two-point distribution, with mean 0 and variance 1. Thus all unpaired marginal observations have identical distributions under U and V, although the proposed coupling interaction differs. Increasing the number of unpaired samples cannot distinguish these models. This is a constructed statistical example, not simulated or observed frog data.

reasoning_steps.argument: Within one stage, let U be uniform on [0,1]. Model I assigns E=U and R=U; Model II assigns E=U and R=1−U. Both models give exactly the same uniform marginal distributions for E and R. However, Var(E)=1/12, while Cov(E,R)=1/12 in Model I and −1/12 in Model II; the coupling slopes are therefore +1 and −1. Independently sampled early and late animals have identical observable distributions under these two models. Thus no analysis of those unlinked measurements alone can distinguish even the sign of individual coupling. Additional unlinked time points do not supply the missing individual correspondence without extra, testable structural assumptions. reasoning_steps.argument: For two stages coded S=0 or 1, suppose every late sample receives its stage's early mean, E=e0+(e1−e0)S. Then S·E=e1S. More biological replicates at the late time improve precision of stage means but do not repair this rank deficiency. reasoning_steps.argument: Consider four equally weighted, registered wound positions. Let early basal injury activity be I=(1,1,0,0). Two possible later local ECM-activity fields are M_A=(1,1,0,0) and M_B=(0,0,1,1). Both have identical activity totals, identical numbers of active positions, and mean activity 1/2. reasoning_steps.argument: For each animal, segment basal epidermal regions j in a preregistered wound region and track their positions from 0.5 to 6 hours. Use equal-area weights and define T=mean_j(I_j*M_j). Define Q=T-E_null(T), where the null reassigns injury measurements among comparable positions within preregistered wound-distance and anatomical strata, preserving the observed marginal fields, cell counts, and geometry. Finite-permutation precision must be reported. This null tests alignment beyond those chosen constraints, not beyond every possible anatomical confound. Injury and ECM probes must be selected and locked before examining regeneration outcomes; neither reporter availability nor specificity is established here.

reasoning_steps.argument: The candidate predicts a positive relationship between Q and subsequent RIC-state induction per eligible basal cell, followed by improved regeneration, conditional on stage, basal-cell abundance, mean injury activity, total ECM activity, and wound closure. Generalized healing predicts that wound closure, viability, or nonspecific wound-associated patterns explain the association. DOI 10.1016/j.ydbio.2021.01.005 and review DOI 10.3390/ijms252111597 are relevant starting references, but their detailed contents have not been inspected. GSE245320 and its component accessions are candidate observational resources, not independent replications.
