Originality and later-publication coverage remain unassessed.
reasoning_steps.title: Scope and prior-art boundary

reasoning_steps.argument: Let E_s(t) denote measured basal-epidermal ERK activity at stage s, C_s(t) denote receptivity to enter the transient regenerative epidermal state, and J_s = k∫E_s(t)C_s(t)dt denote cumulative transition drive, with k > 0. Downstream state occupancy R and remodeling M can be represented by dR/dt = kEC − δ_R R and dM/dt = aR − δ_M M. Model A_amp attributes stage-46 failure to insufficient early E, with C concentrated in the early window at both stages. Model B_delay retains early receptivity at stage 40 but places stage-46 receptivity in the late window. These are deliberately restricted alternatives; broad 'failure to induce RICs' includes both and cannot itself be distinguished by this experiment.
reasoning_steps.title: Define the two restricted competing mechanisms

reasoning_steps.argument: Let p_early and p_late be nonnegative added ERK-activity pulses supported on the respective windows and having the same positive integral Q. Within stage 46, J_late − J_early = k∫C_46(t)[p_late(t) − p_early(t)]dt, because the untreated trajectory cancels. In the idealized A_amp model, C_46 equals c > 0 in the early window and zero in the late window, so the contrast is −kcQ. In B_delay the supports are reversed, giving +kcQ. Thus the sign differs without requiring a difference in total added ERK activity. For nonrectangular receptive windows the contrast measures the pulse-weighted difference in receptivity; its sign is not guaranteed merely by naming a mechanism. A monotone, nonsaturated relationship between transition drive and regrowth transfers this sign to the expected regrowth contrast. Saturation, zero receptivity in both windows or an independent downstream block can erase discrimination.
reasoning_steps.title: Derive the pulse-timing discrimination

reasoning_steps.argument: The proposed stage-46 rescue uses a light-gated RAF/ERK actuator expressed specifically in basal epidermis, comparing early versus late activation. A separate validation cohort must establish expression specificity, ERK activation kinetics, reversibility and noninjurious illumination. Actuator availability and efficacy in these cells are unverified. Measured epidermal ERK trajectories, rather than light duration, define exposure; pulse amplitude and integral should be matched within a preregistered tolerance, provisionally 10%. If endogenous early activity is already near saturation, a larger early light dose is not an adequate matched-exposure control. Failure to achieve comparable perturbations makes the biological contrast uninterpretable and stops the efficacy experiment.
reasoning_steps.title: Specify a feasible intervention class without claiming an available validated reagent

reasoning_steps.argument: At stage 40, transient ERK inhibition during 0.5–2 hours is predicted to reduce the epidermal transition and regrowth more than inhibition during 4.5–6 hours under either restricted model. A reversible MEK inhibitor is an initial implementation candidate, with local delivery preferred; it cannot be described as epidermis-specific without direct validation. Vehicle, washout and epidermal/non-epidermal target-engagement measurements are required. If only systemic inhibition is feasible, the result tests ERK necessity somewhere in the animal, not basal-epidermal necessity. Importantly, stage-46 rescue plus stage-40 blockade alone does not establish a timing gate: the matched early-versus-late rescue contrast supplies the discrimination.
reasoning_steps.title: Use the corresponding block as a necessity control, not a sufficient discriminator

reasoning_steps.argument: The primary efficacy endpoint is blinded day-7 regenerated tail length divided by the standardized length removed, capped at one, with death assigned zero and survival separately reported. This measures an operational regrowth outcome, not complete functional regeneration. Record fin, muscle and axial-tissue organization as secondary endpoints. Define D46 = mean(Y_late rescue) − mean(Y_early rescue). A preregistered biologically relevant target is D46 ≥ 0.25 for B_delay or D46 ≤ −0.25 for A_amp, together with a 95% confidence interval excluding zero; these numbers are design thresholds, not estimated effects. Require that the favored rescue also improves over vehicle, since a positive contrast caused only by early-treatment damage is not rescue. Intermediate outcomes are epidermal ERK trajectories, RIC-state induction per basal-epidermal cell, absolute epidermal cell abundance, and subsequent ECM remodeling. Sampling at 0, 0.5, 2, 4.5, 6, 12 and 24 hours brackets the proposed windows; these are new experimental sampling times, not asserted GEO coverage. A single 6-hour state measurement is inadequate because different decay times after the two pulses can mimic different induction.
reasoning_steps.title: Predefine outcomes and numerical decision targets

reasoning_steps.argument: First run a feasibility pilot of 12 animals per efficacy arm, balanced across four clutches, solely to evaluate manipulation and assay validity. The six proposed efficacy arms are stage-46 vehicle, early rescue and late rescue, and stage-40 vehicle, early block and late block. A provisional confirmatory size is 64 animals per arm across eight new clutches. For an independently randomized bounded outcome in [0,1], variance is at most 0.25; the conventional two-group normal approximation gives n ≈ 2(1.96+0.84)^2(0.25)/(0.25)^2 = 62.72 per arm for 80% power against a 0.25 difference at two-sided 0.05. This is a planning approximation, not a guarantee under clutch heterogeneity, discrete outcomes or multiple confirmatory comparisons. Pilot-informed simulation and a frozen analysis plan must precede final enrollment. Randomize individual animals within clutch and developmental stage; avoid treatment-specific shared tanks. If exposure is tank-level, the tank becomes the randomized unit and this animal-level calculation is invalid. Cells and image fields are subsamples, never independent animals.
reasoning_steps.title: Bound sample size and preserve biological units

reasoning_steps.argument: Include wounded vehicle controls, light-only actuator-negative controls, actuator-positive no-light controls, and unamputated treatment controls for toxicity and developmental effects. Standardize amputation plane, staging criteria, feeding, density, temperature and observation time; blind scoring and balance processing batches. Quantify wound closure, epidermal viability and tissue composition so that apparent RIC loss is not merely cell depletion. ERK pulses could rescue through generic growth rather than induction of the proposed epidermal state: rescue without a preceding state-transition change contradicts this specified mediation model. A persistent cell-intrinsic RIC-state block predicts neither early nor late rescue despite target engagement, but that outcome is also compatible with a downstream block or an incorrect tested window. It therefore rejects the bounded two-window rescue hypothesis, not every possible timing mechanism.
reasoning_steps.title: Counterfactual controls and alternative explanations

reasoning_steps.argument: Before using GEO data, verify sample identities, pooling, biological replicates, units, processing batches and stage-by-time coverage. Cross-sectional bulk samples cannot establish an individual animal's early-to-late coupling, and predominantly regenerating scRNA-seq cannot supply missing matched refractory trajectories. In new specimens, a nonlethal validated ERK/state reporter would permit within-animal temporal measurements followed by day-7 scoring; otherwise molecular companion cohorts support only group-level mediation. Any predictive analysis must compare stage-only, RIC/ECM-only and known-signaling baselines with the timing interaction on held-out clutches, using animal-level uncertainty. A later naturally regained-competence stage, chosen only after confirming X. laevis staging and husbandry behavior, provides an additional independent condition: recovery of early receptivity would support a reversible timing explanation, whereas its absence narrows or contradicts that explanation. Include timing, appropriate sham and injury controls, toxicity, stage matching, sample size assumptions and a quantitative primary endpoint such as blinded morphologic regeneration score at a specified post-amputation time. Identify ethical/laboratory requirements; the software must not claim experiments were conducted.

strategy_runs.current_question: Revise the pulse-timing test to distinguish wound-age-dependent gating from stage-dependent response kinetics: define vehicle-adjusted responses at matched elapsed times after early and late pulses, retain a common post-amputation endpoint, specify a timing-invariant within-stage kinetic null and its falsifying contrast, and state exposure, viability and precision stop conditions. Treat this solely as a design revision; do not invent source access, measurements or novelty evidence.

strategy_runs.strategy_text: Attempt to refute the leading candidate by literature search, baseline models, alternate time windows, batch-aware resampling and a genuinely independent cohort or independently generated perturbation/phenotype dataset if accessible. Define the outcome as verified mechanism, replicated computational association, novel unverified hypothesis or unresolved failure. Check that the proposed prediction was not used to select the validation data and quantify uncertainty. No positive biological-mechanism claim without independent biological validation.

strategy_text: Build a sourced evidence ledger through 2026 for the Xenopus laevis refractory period, RIC formation, matrix remodeling, immune/ROS signals, signaling pathways, and nutritional influences. Retrieve GSE245320 metadata and verify exactly which developmental stages, time points, biological replicates and technologies exist; identify any phenotype-labeled independent datasets. Search explicitly for the proposed interaction in prior literature. Do not treat RIC, ECM or metabolic associations as novel discoveries. Stop when the new-versus-known boundary and possible falsifiable gap are unambiguous.
